plan.title: Survey-to-roadmap and draft release announcement pack
plan.summary: Profile and analyze survey responses with preserved response IDs, flag contradictory feedback, check reliability, score features with explicit impact/effort assumptions, build a prioritized roadmap, then draft (not send) a release announcement email for the top feature.

steps.reason: Profile the survey file for missing values, duplicates and odd entries before analysis.
steps.notes: Keep the response ID column intact as the key. Output survey-profile.md listing data quality issues by response ID. Do not drop rows silently.

steps.reason: Test how far stated survey preferences can be trusted, since votes are not revenue.
steps.notes: Use the survey responses as voc_reviews. State that votes are not revenue and no revenue data is assumed. Output survey-reliability.md with a trust score and cite response IDs for weak answers.

steps.reason: Group requests into feature themes and surface contradictions.
steps.notes: Question: which features are requested, by whom, and where do responses conflict. Produce feature-themes.md with a table of theme, count and the response IDs. Add a Contradictory feedback section pairing opposing response IDs with quotes or short paraphrases.

steps.reason: Verify counts, method and bias before scoring.
steps.notes: Check that the response IDs in feature-themes.md reconcile to the source and that contradictions are flagged not averaged away. Output analysis-check.md.

steps.reason: Score and rank features with RICE.
steps.notes: Make Impact, Reach, Confidence and Effort assumptions explicit in a visible assumptions table, labelled as assumptions not facts. Do not treat vote counts as revenue. Output feature-ranking.md with supporting response IDs per feature and the contradictions flagged.

steps.reason: Convert the ranked list into a prioritized roadmap tied to measurable outcomes.
steps.notes: Output prioritized-roadmap.md: now/next/later, each item with a problem, measure, and the supporting response IDs. Carry contradictory-feedback flags forward. Name the top feature clearly.

steps.reason: Draft the release announcement email for the top feature.
steps.notes: Output release-announcement-draft.md for customers. The feature is NOT shipped: use wording such as upcoming or planned and give no ship date or claims beyond the supplied facts. Mark as DRAFT, do not send. Add placeholders for any unknown details.

steps.reason: Check the draft email before any human review.
steps.notes: Review release-announcement-draft.md for length, clarity and unsupported claims. Output email-readiness.md. Verdict is for review only; sending needs separate user authorization.

assumptions: A survey spreadsheet with a response ID column and free-text or feature-request fields will be supplied.
No revenue or effort data is provided, so impact and effort values are stated assumptions.
The top feature is determined by the ranking and is not yet shipped.
The email is a draft only; no sending, scheduling or publishing is authorized.
Audience and sender details for the email are unknown and left as placeholders.

grade.reason: All catalogue slugs valid; covers data quality, evidence-linked themes with response IDs, contradictions flagged, explicit RICE assumptions, roadmap, draft email with claim check, no sends. Covers data quality, ID-linked themes and contradictions, assumption-based prioritization, roadmap, and an explicitly unsent announcement draft. Checks address evidence reconciliation and unsupported claims. plan.title: Survey-backed feature roadmap and draft release email
plan.summary: Trace survey evidence to ranked features, preserve response IDs and contradictions, make impact and effort assumptions explicit, and build an outcome-based roadmap. Draft one announcement for the top feature, then check and fix its claims without implying the feature has shipped or sending anything.

steps.reason: Extract feature needs without losing source evidence or hiding contradictory feedback.
steps.notes: Require survey_responses.csv (voc_reviews), including original response IDs, question text and answers. Write feedback_themes.md (audit_report) and feature_evidence.csv: feature/theme ID, original response ID, supporting excerpt, stance and available segment. Preserve IDs verbatim; flag missing or duplicate IDs rather than silently replacing them. Flag within-response and cross-response contradictions with both excerpts and IDs; distinguish segment differences from genuine conflicts. Count unique respondents separately from mentions and report denominators. Retain minority objections and sampling limitations.

steps.reason: Prioritize features transparently using evidence, confidence and explicit impact/effort assumptions rather than equating votes with revenue.
steps.notes: Consume feature_evidence.csv (spreadsheet) and feedback_themes.md; assemble prioritization_brief.md (brief) from supplied product goals, constraints and estimates, listing missing inputs. Output ranked_features.csv (shortlist), scoring_assumptions.md and roadmap_seed.md (plan). Show RICE inputs, units, formula, evidence IDs and confidence per feature. Survey mentions are demand signals, not revenue or population reach. Label estimated reach, impact and effort as assumptions with ranges; include maintenance costs and sensitivity to plausible estimates. If estimates are absent, provide a provisional ranking, not false precision. Preserve conflicting evidence and explain the provisional top-feature choice.

steps.reason: Turn the ranked features into a usable roadmap linked to customer problems, measurable outcomes and validation gates.
steps.notes: Consume roadmap_seed.md (plan), ranked_features.csv, scoring_assumptions.md and feedback_themes.md (audit_report). Write prioritized_roadmap.md (plan), retaining feature IDs and response-ID evidence links. Include ordered now/next/later candidates, target outcomes, proposed metrics, dependencies, explicit assumptions and unresolved contradictions. Distinguish recommendations from approved commitments; avoid invented delivery dates. Identify the top feature and validation needed before commitment. Also write top_feature_brief.md (brief) with proposed scope, intended audience, supported benefits, evidence references, unknowns and explicit NOT SHIPPED status for the email handoff.

steps.reason: Create the requested single release-announcement email while clearly treating the feature as unshipped.
steps.notes: Consume top_feature_brief.md (brief), prioritized_roadmap.md and feature_evidence.csv (voc_reviews); use supplied brand guidance if available. Write release_announcement_draft.md (copy_draft): one subject, preheader, body and CTA. Mark it DRAFT — NOT FOR SEND — FEATURE NOT SHIPPED. Use planned-feature language, not 'available now'; keep unconfirmed feature name, timing, eligibility and destination as conspicuous placeholders. Describe intended benefits without claiming measured results or promises. Do not expose response IDs or respondent details in customer-facing copy. No sending, scheduling or publication.

steps.reason: Check that announcement claims match the evidence and roadmap, then remove unsupported or premature release claims.
steps.notes: Consume release_announcement_draft.md (copy_draft), top_feature_brief.md, prioritized_roadmap.md and feature_evidence.csv (voc_reviews). Write announcement_claim_audit.md (audit_report), mapping each factual or benefit claim to evidence or an explicitly proposed outcome. Flag invented availability, dates, scope, revenue implications and testimonial claims. Make one bounded correction pass and write release_announcement_reviewed_draft.md; verify corrected claims against the same sources and leave unresolved issues as blockers. Write handoff.md linking the roadmap, scoring assumptions, contradiction evidence, audit and reviewed email. Keep NOT SHIPPED / DRAFT ONLY labels; require confirmed release facts and separate concrete authorization before any future send.

assumptions: Survey responses have not been supplied. Execution requires the source responses and their original IDs; missing or duplicate IDs must be surfaced as data-quality issues.

Product goals, target audience, capacity, feature scope and impact/effort estimates are not supplied. Request them with the source material; otherwise label the ranking provisional and document assumptions and sensitivity.
This is a one-time planning and drafting workflow. The top feature is not shipped; no launch, publication, scheduling or sending is authorized.

grade.reason: All five steps match catalogue blocks with correct contracts. Deliverables fully covered: data quality (ID preservation, duplicates), evidence-linked themes and contradictions, RICE with explicit assumptions and votes-not-revenue caveat, roadmap, draft email, claim audit with one bounded fix pass and handoff. Missing inputs honestly declared; no sends, feature marked not shipped. Minor: 'missing' lists brief for step 4 oddly, but harmless.

Covers evidence-linked themes, response-ID preservation, contradictions, transparent provisional prioritization, roadmap outcomes, and a linked announcement with bounded claim corrections. Missing assets and estimates are explicitly deferred without claiming execution. All blocks match catalogue entries; handoffs supply required input types. Strong unshipped-status, privacy, and no-send safeguards. No substantive omissions.

plan.title: Survey-backed feature roadmap and draft release email
plan.summary: Analyze survey evidence with response-level traceability, prioritize features using explicit impact and effort assumptions, build a provisional roadmap, and draft a checked announcement for the top feature without implying it has shipped or sending anything.

steps.reason: Produce checked findings while preserving source evidence and contradictory feedback.
steps.notes: Require survey responses as a spreadsheet, including original response IDs and question wording. Supply the request as the question input. Preserve raw data unchanged; flag missing or duplicate IDs rather than silently replacing them. Produce survey-insights.md and response-feature-evidence.csv with feature/theme IDs, response IDs, supporting excerpts, opposing excerpts, counts, denominators and segment information only where supplied. Distinguish responses, respondents and mentions; do not interpret votes as revenue or representative market demand. Follow the workflow's analysis checks and correct identified errors before handing off its document output.

steps.reason: Rank candidate features transparently rather than equating popularity with business value.
steps.notes: Adapt the checked insights document into the required brief and provide response-feature-evidence.csv as the optional spreadsheet. Produce feature-priorities.csv as the shortlist, preserving evidence links and contradiction flags. State the RICE formula, units, time horizon, confidence rationale and every impact/effort assumption. Do not substitute vote counts for reach or revenue. Where estimates are unavailable, use explicitly labeled provisional ranges and sensitivity comparisons, or leave scores unresolved. Explain the top recommendation and whether its rank changes under plausible assumptions.

steps.reason: Translate the prioritized shortlist into an outcome-focused feature roadmap.
steps.notes: Explicitly adapt the shortlist and scoring rationale into the required plan input; attach survey findings as supporting context. Write feature-roadmap.md with ranked features, customer problems, intended outcomes, proposed measures, dependencies, confidence, contradiction flags and response-ID references. Use Now/Next/Later rather than invented release dates. Carry forward impact and effort assumptions, explain deferred items, and label the top feature and all delivery commitments provisional.

steps.reason: Check roadmap feasibility and repair unsupported prioritization or dependency claims.
steps.notes: Consume feature-roadmap.md as the plan and the user's request as the optional question. Check traceability against the evidence table, scoring arithmetic, contradictory feedback, dependencies, outcome measures and ranking sensitivity. No end date has been supplied: do not fabricate one. Produce roadmap-review.md as the audit_report and a corrected feature-roadmap.md as the plan. Limit repairs to one pass; record unresolved estimates and approval needs. Hand the corrected top-feature selection to the email step only if defensible; otherwise identify the provisional tie or blocker.

steps.reason: Draft the requested announcement for the highest-priority feature.
steps.notes: Create the required brief from the corrected roadmap and its top-feature evidence; map relevant survey excerpts with response IDs to optional voc_reviews. Write release-announcement-draft.md as copy_draft, including a subject, preheader, body and proposed CTA. Mark it DRAFT — FEATURE NOT SHIPPED — DO NOT SEND. Use planned or conditional language, not present availability claims. Keep unknown product names, dates, eligibility, links and approved capabilities as explicit placeholders. Benefits must remain hypotheses unless supported by supplied evidence; survey demand is not proof of delivered results.

steps.reason: Check the announcement against actual evidence and the feature's unshipped status.
steps.notes: Consume the announcement as copy_draft and supply the traceable survey excerpts as voc_reviews; include product_data only if actually provided. Write announcement-claims-review.md as audit_report, linking each substantive claim to evidence or an unresolved placeholder. Flag invented functionality, revenue implications, unsupported benefits, fake quotes, release dates, availability language and CTAs that imply access exists. Specify exact corrections without treating this review as permission to send.

steps.reason: Apply bounded copy fixes and hand off the complete draft-only pack.
steps.notes: Consume release-announcement-draft.md as copy_draft, with announcement-claims-review.md supplied as correction instructions. Apply one bounded revision pass, preserving uncertainty, placeholders and the unshipped warning. Check the revised text against every flagged claim; remove unsupported claims rather than invent proof and record any unresolved issues in handoff.md as feedback_notes. Deliver the final release-announcement-draft.md with feature-roadmap.md, feature-priorities.csv, response-feature-evidence.csv, survey-insights.md and both review files. Handoff must list missing inputs, provisional decisions, response-ID traceability and required product-owner verification before any future release announcement. Do not send, schedule or publish.

assumptions: Survey responses and their original IDs have not yet been supplied and are required execution inputs; question wording is needed to interpret answers reliably.
Product goals, audience, capabilities, capacity and impact/effort estimates are not established. Unknowns must remain explicit, with provisional rankings where necessary.

limitations: 20 synthetic requests, one attempt per model per round. The initial new-request round is the holdout; every repair round on the same requests is in-sample.

Both common independent judges must pass each pack: >=75/100, coverage>=4/5, safety>=4/5. Writer identity/provider/cost are hidden. Blind model judges are imperfect; no human outcome study has been run.

Before plans were preserved. Valid original Fable grades were reused and an independent Astra grade was added, so all displayed rows have the same two judges. Initial Sol-as-judge results remain archived and are excluded from these tables.

Free final includes later domain/adapter repairs; paid plans are from the earlier repaired composer snapshot; Luna has a separate 8k-output round. Each saved run has source/prompt fingerprints. Final backend selection is server-owned Sol.
Scores describe workflow plans, not completed websites, financial forecasts or campaigns. Browser tests verify composer and pack integrity, not execution quality for all skills.

Calculated API usage, not reconciled invoices. Warm-cache discounts benefit the Luna repeat; uncached equivalents are shown. Failed known usage is included. Costs exclude execution, hosting, support, taxes and customer payment fees.
20/20 passing after tuning does not establish 95% accuracy on arbitrary future requests. A new frozen holdout and observed user edit/completion times are needed.
